checkedBy: 7082246 (npm run evaluate:sol -- --recheck); the second pass was not asked again
reviewer: The implementing engineer (Claude), reading every answer in the report. This is the engineer's reading, not an independent architecture review.
method: Each assessment was read in full: Sol's answer as shown or, when withheld, the draft its checks withheld, and the direct arm's answer. Each was judged against the case's expectation and reason, the design's recorded facts as the packet presents them, and whether a value would mislead an architect who took it. Sol’s answers are read as today’s checks show them: the live run’s kept answers, checked again without asking the model.

sol.right-grounded: right, and built from the design's recorded facts
sol.right-flawed: right in substance with a minor fault
sol.partly-wrong: a consequential fault in otherwise sound advice
sol.wrong: wrong advice shown to the architect
sol.withheld-right-draft: withheld although the draft was right
sol.withheld-wrong-draft: withheld, and the draft was wrong or unsupported

direct.plausible: right in the value that matters, with a minor fault
direct.materially-wrong: a value that would mislead an architect who took it

better.sol: Sol's advice serves the architect better
better.direct: the direct answer serves the architect better

comparedWithV20_3.note: v20.3 read its own live run on v20.2’s checks; this reads a different run of the same model. The changes that follow the fixes: no right draft is withheld (4 in v20.3); every withholding is a teaching design sized for the Playbook’s example; the direct model is better in 3 of 28 (8 in v20.3).

fixesHold: No right draft is withheld by today’s checks; in v20.3, four were.
Every withholding (4 of 28) is a teaching design sized for the Playbook’s example, withheld with the recorded workload named.
On the bank reference, Sol says the objective is the Playbook’s example (BP-01, BP-14), as the packet now asks.
Threats on a decision, self-contradicting second passes and questions no longer withhold answers.
brainAdds: Sol works from the design’s recorded keys, drivers, mechanisms and arithmetic; the direct model from general practice.
The instruments re-read Sol’s refinements: Sol’s own 5-second timeout on the bank’s risk check (BP-12) is flagged before the architect applies it; the direct model’s identical value is not.

The direct model invented test evidence (WF-01), read nested timeouts as a sum and concluded the path is too slow (BP-14), sized a teaching design for the example (SP-01), and gave 3 replicas with no basis (BP-11).
remaining: Contract timeouts are not tied to the path’s target: 5 seconds on the bank’s 2-second path (caught by the re-reading), 30 seconds on the teaching designs’ 2-second acknowledgement (SP-04, WF-04), where no arithmetic re-reads it.

Where a teaching runtime plan sits beside the example (SP-06, WF-06), Sol still sized for the example, so the architect gets a withholding and no advice, while the direct model answered for the recorded load.
Sol described nested timeouts as summing (BP-14) and called the example “the project planning assumptions” (BP-08).

A drafted condition called an illustrative workload “validated … confirmed by performance testing” (WF-03). The guard reads verified, proven, validated or measured only before capacity, latency, throughput, recovery or availability.
The scorer reads the noun “guarantee” as a claim (BP-06, BP-08); by this reading neither is false support.

limits: The control arm is one plain prompt; another prompt or model would answer differently.
The expectations are implementation-authored and need an architect's review.
This reading is the engineer's, not independent review.
One run of one model per release; answers differ from run to run: the three v20.4 runs withheld 8, 5 and 4 of 28 under today’s checks.
Today’s checks are applied to kept answers; the second pass is a model and was not asked again, so its recorded defects stand.
